edits.before: 这时的国会人很少。同一天，有议员动议先问一个问题：七个州出席的国会，是否有权接受总司令的辞职？日志留下了点名表决：名单上列出的议员几乎都投赞成，帕特里奇投了反对，埃勒里则应本人要求把反对改成了赞成。22日的出席记录是马萨诸塞、罗得岛、宾夕法尼亚、特拉华、马里兰、弗吉尼亚和北卡罗来纳七个州，另有新罕布什尔和南卡罗来纳各一名议员。到了23日接见当天上午，国会还议决立即写信给新罕布什尔、康涅狄格、纽约、新泽西、南卡罗来纳和佐治亚六个州的行政长官，催他们的代表马上到会：国会在此开会期间，出席的从未超过七个州，其中多数只有两名代表，而批准正式和约等几件要务都需要至少九个州同意。
edits.after: 这时的国会人很少。同一天，日志记下一个付诸表决的问题：七个州出席的国会，是否有权接受总司令的辞职？日志留下了点名表决：名单上列出的议员几乎都投赞成，帕特里奇投了反对；埃勒里的反对票，日志记为应“该议员”的请求改成了赞成，没有写明这位议员是谁。22日的出席记录是马萨诸塞、罗得岛、宾夕法尼亚、特拉华、马里兰、弗吉尼亚和北卡罗来纳七个州，另有新罕布什尔和南卡罗来纳各一名议员。到了23日接见当天，国会还议决立即写信给新罕布什尔、康涅狄格、纽约、新泽西、南卡罗来纳和佐治亚六个州的行政长官，催他们的代表马上到会：国会在此开会期间，出席的从未超过七个州，其中多数只有两名代表，而批准正式和约等几件要务都需要至少九个州同意。

edits.before: Congress was thin at the time. The same day, a motion asked a prior question: "Is it the sense of Congress that seven states in Congress Assembled are competent to receive the resignation of a Commander in Chief?" The journal kept the roll call. Nearly every member listed voted ay; Partridge voted no, and Ellery's no was changed into ay at his own request. On the 22nd the states present were Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia and North Carolina, with one member each from New Hampshire and South Carolina. And on the morning of the audience itself, the 23rd, Congress resolved to write at once to the executives of New Hampshire, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, South Carolina and Georgia, demanding the immediate attendance of their delegates: during the sitting at this place there had never been more than seven states represented, most of them by only two delegates, and the ratification of the definitive treaty, among other matters, required the assent of at least nine states.

edits.before: The agreed order of the audience ran to three clauses. First, the President and the members were to sit, covered — that is, wearing their hats — with the secretary standing at the President's side. Second, the General's arrival was to be announced to the secretary by a messenger, who would then introduce the General, attended by his aides, into the Hall of Congress. Third, the secretary would conduct the General to a chair and he would be seated, an aide standing on either side of him, while the secretary resumed his own place. Sitters, hat-wearers, standers, entrants: everyone had an assigned position.

First, the President and the members were to sit, covered — that is, wearing their hats — with the secretary standing at the President's side. Second, the General's arrival was to be announced by a messenger to the secretary, and the secretary would then introduce the General, attended by his aides, into the Hall of Congress. Third, the secretary would conduct the General to a chair and he would be seated, an aide standing on either side of him, while the secretary resumed his own place. Sitters, hat-wearers, standers, entrants: everyone had an assigned position.

edits.before: Set this handover beside an ordinary spoken one and three things are happening at once. First, the sequence was fixed in advance: agreed on the twenty-second, carried out on the twenty-third, with no record of last-minute adjustment. Second, the etiquette was asymmetric: the General was to bow when he rose to speak and when he withdrew, and Congress to answer by uncovering: the standing man bowed, the seated body answered. The vertical distance between them was kept deliberately visible. Third, what changed hands was physical: the commission, plus a copy of the address. Ceremony, posture, and token together make up this documented transfer of power.
